svg.text: Tip everything out and match each thing to a picture. Read the tiny printed letters on the small boards; they are how you tell the pins apart.
The computer. Two black strips of sockets along the long edges. Tiny numbers at the strip ends.
Hold it by the edges. The side with the microSD slot and dog logo is the side you use.
Plastic slab of holes. Red and blue lines mark the power rails.
Half size (30 columns) or mini (17): either works.
Must be a data cable. A charge-only cable looks identical
and is the most common reason nothing works.
Fingernail-sized, 4 pins (some have 6). Reads VIN or VCC,
GND, SCL, SDA. Measures temperature, pressure, humidity.
Pins point down here; on yours they may be on any edge.
Small dark glass on a board, 4 pins on the top edge. VCC, GND, SCL,
SDA, but the order of the first two varies. Read yours and write it
Has a round coin cell holder. 6 pins on one edge. Uses SCL, SDA, VCC, GND only.
Leave it in the bag on your first build. No battery until you read HARDWARE.md.
Jumper wires, male to male (a pin at both ends)
Colours are a convention: any four colours
work if you use them consistently. Pick
and write them down before you start.
Not needed and not in the bag: a screen, keyboard or power supply for the board. Your laptop is all three, over the USB-C cable.
